issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Failed Role: I have failed in my most important role in life
issues.explanation: For a 35-year-old single male special education teacher reporting a mugging/robbery, 'I have failed in my most important role in life' is hard to link coherently to the rest of the profile. The other appraisals center on self-blame and persistent danger, but this item implies a salient role failure theme (e.g. partner/parent/protector) that is not otherwise represented in triggers, threat, or memory.

issues.item: Memory: Shame on Recall: When I remember the event I feel intense shame
issues.explanation: Within Memory, intense shame and intense rage on recall can coexist, but paired with a mugging/robbery and the rest of this profile they pull toward different meanings of the event without enough support elsewhere. Shame would usually connect to strong self-blame/humiliation themes, while rage would connect to injustice/anger themes; the profile does not integrate both clearly.

vignette: Aleksei had always felt a sense of purpose in his work as a special education teacher. He took pride in creating a safe and supportive environment for his students, many of whom struggled with their own challenges. But all of that changed on a typical Wednesday evening, when Aleksei was walking home from the grocery store. As he turned a corner, he was suddenly grabbed from behind and dragged into an alleyway by two strangers. They demanded his wallet and phone, and in the ensuing struggle, Aleksei's neck was wrenched to one side, leaving him with a searing pain that would linger for weeks. The mugging lasted only minutes, but its impact has been felt for months. Aleksei can still recall every detail of the attack with photographic clarity - the feel of rough hands on his skin, the sound of his own voice begging for mercy, the sight of his attackers' faces twisted in anger. When these memories surface, as they often do, Aleksei is flooded with intense rage and guilt. He replays the event over and over in his mind, wondering what he could have done differently to avoid it. Somebody else, he thinks, would not have walked down that street at that time; somebody else would have been more aware of their surroundings. As a result, Aleksei has become hyper-vigilant, constantly scanning for potential threats. He finds himself checking the locks on his apartment door multiple times before bed, and scouring the crowded hallways of his school for suspicious faces. Even in familiar settings, he feels compelled to identify escape routes, mentally rehearsing the steps he would take if danger were to strike again. The presence of authority figures only heightens Aleksei's anxiety. When police officers visit his classroom to talk to students about safety, he feels a surge of tension, as if their uniforms and badges are somehow linked to the traumatic event. He begins to sweat and fidget in his seat, his mind racing with worst-case scenarios. The triggers are everywhere, it seems. A shouted comment from a student can transport Aleksei back to that alleyway, where he is once again helpless and afraid. And when his neck pain flares up, as it often does after a long day of teaching, Aleksei is convinced that he is reliving the attack all over again. Aleksei's inability to relax has become a defining feature of his daily life. Even in quiet moments, when he knows he is safe, his body remains on high alert, primed for flight or fight. He feels like he is constantly waiting for the other shoe to drop, for some new threat to emerge from the shadows. As the months have passed, Aleksei's avoidance behaviors have begun to take a toll on his relationships and daily routines. He has stopped attending staff meetings, citing " neck pain" as an excuse, and has become withdrawn in social situations, where he fears being overwhelmed by loud noises or crowded spaces. His students have noticed the change in him, too - he seems distant, preoccupied, and less patient than before. It was only when Aleksei's principal expressed concern about his performance that he realized he needed help. He couldn't keep living like this, constantly on edge, unable to shake the memories of that fateful night. With a sense of trepidation, Aleksei made an appointment with a therapist, hoping to find some way to break free from the cycle of fear and anxiety that had consumed his life.
